items.title: Day list: which days have SD recordings
items.facts: searchDateWithVideo over the control channel (local HTTPS :443 multipleRequest, or cloud passthrough). Dates are yyyyMMdd, channel is a list [0]. Windows asks one month-sized range per calendar page. Response playback.search_results is a list of single-key maps whose item has date yyyyMMdd; result is a sorted set of dates. Invalid or non-8-digit date raises a protocol error.

items.title: Clip list of one local day (searchVideoWithUTC, paged)
items.facts: Day window is local midnight to midnight+86399 as UTC epoch seconds (timezone of the TV, DST-days are 23/25 h in the timeline but the query uses +86399 from local midnight). Page size 100 via start_index/end_index (0..99, 100..199); continue while playback.to_be_continued != 0 and the page is non-empty; safety cap 100 pages. Result clips sorted by start. Items are single-key maps with startTime/endTime (int or numeric string, UTC s) and video_type or misspelled vedio_type (string). Missing type = 0. Types: 1 timing, 2 motion, 6 person, others per spec enum.

items.title: -71103 fallback: retry clip search with player_id
items.facts: Some firmware (C510W) answers the legacy form with error -71103. The client retries that page once with the same request where key id:1 is replaced by player_id (32 lower-case hex), and remembers the working form for later calls on that client. A second -71103 is raised to the caller. player_id for remote clients is the terminal uuid when it is 32 hex, else a stable per-process uuid4 hex.

items.title: Choose playback transport: local :8800 or relay
items.facts: Transport is relay when the camera is cloud-routed (remote, shared role 1, offline on LAN) and a signed-in relay provider exists; otherwise local :8800. Shared cameras on the LAN still use the relay. When neither works the state is FAILED with a reason: not on this network, camera offline, shared camera cloud only. Search calls follow the same routing (local control client vs cloud passthrough RemoteControlClient with player_id). Playback and live view each use one of the camera's two media sessions (same limiter key).

items.title: Range playback request (get playback)
items.facts: One get playback request from the chosen start second to end_utc (normally end of the local day). Times are strings of UTC epoch seconds, start must be > 0, end >= start. client_id 1, channels [0], scale always '1/1' (only verified value), event_type [1,2] (timing + motion). seq is added by the session (incrementing from 1). Camera then plays the following recordings of the range one after another. Reply is type response with result {error_code, session_id, speed}; success is error_code 0 and a non-empty session_id; a missing session_id falls back to the media parts' X-Session-Id. Start/seek inside a gap snaps to the start of the next clip (to the requested time when no later clip).

items.title: SD playback over local :8800
items.facts: Same persistent POST /stream session as live view: Digest handshake, boundary --client-stream-boundary-- (client) and --device-stream-boundary-- (device), Key-Exchange (MD5 or HKDF keys, AES-128-CBC parts, X-Data-Hmac) as in the live-view lane. After connect send the get playback request. Device parts: video/mp2t (MPEG-TS, forward to the player) and application/json (notifications). Ack every 25 parts with the stream_sequence notification. Playback uses the cloud password or the local access token like live view; connection loss reconnects and resumes with a new request at the last position. Camera refusing with a non-zero error_code is fatal (no retry loop) to protect the camera.
items.target: lib/api/vod_session.dart + android RelayBridge-style loopback feeding LivePlayer.kt (plain MPEG-TS)

items.title: SD playback through the cloud relay (remote/shared)
items.facts: Relay slot request with streamType 1 (playback; 3 is download, preview is live), channelId '0', customParams '{}', cloudType 2 (1 gives -1007). Tunnel is plaintext MPEG-TS parts with no inner POST /stream: first a get playback JSON part, then video/mp2t parts, ack every 25 parts, heartbeat every 15 s. Every start, seek or reconnect takes a NEW relay slot. The relay closes the tunnel after the last recording instead of sending 'finished'; treat position >= last clip end - 1.5 s as end. Verified on a real remote C510W (392 parts for a 66 s clip in 15 s). Stop request is do stop 'null'.

items.title: Pause, resume, seek, speed
items.facts: Pause: client holds the next frame, sends do pause 'null'. Resume: do play 'null'. If the camera dropped the paused connection the normal reconnect resumes from the last position. Seek = a fresh get playback at the new second (the in-session do play {start_time} seek is in the spec but unverified on real firmware); also resumes a paused playback and restarts after end of recordings. Speed: allowed 1/1, 2/1, 4/1, 8/1; the request always asks 1/1 and speed is applied client-side by pacing frames (limited by link throughput). Cameras send faster than real time while acked, so pacing by PTS is required.

items.title: Position tracking from TS PTS
items.facts: Recording time is derived from the video PES PTS (90 kHz, 33-bit wrap). Steps 0..3 s advance the position; a larger or backwards step means a new recording file and the position jumps to the start of the next clip of the day's list; running past a clip end + 1.5 s moves to the next clip start. Without a clip list and step < 86400 s the position advances anyway. Position callback about 5 times a second. Parts that are not whole 188-byte aligned TS packets are paced by the X-Data-PTS header. Needed so the TV can show a cursor on the 24 h timeline when ExoPlayer only sees a continuous TS.

items.title: End of recordings and notifications
items.facts: Camera notification stream_status status 'finished' ends the requested range. If a later clip of the day exists a new request starts there (continuous playback), otherwise state STOPPED with reason 'end of recordings'. disk_status offline = SD card not available (fatal). Relay ends by closing the tunnel (see relay item). Other notifications: playback_switch_next, heartbeat, connection_closed, stream_finish(reason). Behaviour across clip boundaries and at the end is NOT verified on hardware (AGENTS.md section 8), TV must tolerate both finished and plain close.

items.title: Day picker and 24 h timeline on TV
items.facts: Player screen has a Day control (max date = tomorrow), a timeline bar of the LOCAL day with recorded segments, hour ticks and a cursor. local_day_range gives local midnight to next local midnight (23 or 25 h on DST days). Selecting a day stops playback, reloads that day's clips and starts at the first clip; no clips shows 'No recordings on this day'. Click/drag on the timeline seeks (drag seeks on release). Next/previous clip buttons jump by clip start; speed combobox 1x,2x,4x,8x. Playback request end = max(end of day, start+1). TV adaptation: D-pad left/right = coarse seek by clip or +-30 s, up/down picks day, OK toggles pause; month grid calls the day list once per month.

items.title: Clip download (not needed on TV for P0)
items.facts: Windows downloads a clip to MP4 via get download (local) or relay streamType 3 with subType 'cover' (not verified on hardware) falling back to the playback stream (proven). Not required for TV playback; defer.

items.title: Motion notifications without a camera account: poll getLastAlarmInfo
items.facts: Windows tray notifications come from AppController.motion_event, fed by service.start_events. Choice: (1) cloud-routed camera (remote/shared): poll getLastAlarmInfo through cloud passthrough, interval max(5 s, 30 s) = 30 s; (2) LAN camera without a camera (third) account: poll getLastAlarmInfo over local HTTPS every 5 s; (3) LAN camera with a camera account: ONVIF PullPoint on :2020. No cloud/msg push is used. Poller: first reading is a baseline (no event); each later change of last_alarm_time emits one active event with type last_alarm_type (motion, person...); timestamp from last_alarm_time epoch string else now; topic 'tapo:LastAlarmInfo/<type or motion>'; source last_alarm_info. Errors are logged (1st, 10th, every 60th) and polling continues. Request is a plain control call with no secrets.

items.title: Motion toast / PiP
items.facts: Tray shows a toast (title = camera name, text 'Motion detected at <time>' or 'Motion detected') only for active events of known cameras, only when setting notifications is true, and at most one per camera every 10 s (clock based). Inactive events and unknown camera ids never toast. TV: lib/ui/motion_pip_toast.dart shows a transient overlay card (optionally a live PiP of that camera) with the same throttle and setting, no tray.

items.title: ONVIF PullPoint flow (only with a camera account)
items.facts: Port 2020, SOAP 1.2, POST with Content-Type application/soap+xml; charset=utf-8, one short connection per call, 8 MiB response cap. Steps: GetCapabilities (device service /onvif/device_service) to find the events XAddr path (fallback /onvif/service); CreatePullPointSubscription with InitialTerminationTime PT60S; SubscriptionReference/Address gives the path+query used for later calls and the wsa:To value; loop PullMessages (Timeout PT5S, MessageLimit 10, wsa:Action PullMessagesRequest) with a network timeout of pull timeout + socket timeout; Renew (wsnt:TerminationTime PT60S, Action RenewRequest) when the renew deadline passes (renew margin max(10 s, pull+net+2) capped at ttl/2); remaining ttl = TerminationTime - CurrentTime of the camera clock; Unsubscribe best effort (2 s) on stop or fault. Any failure re-subscribes with backoff doubling from 1 s up to 30 s. A callback exception must not stop the loop.

items.title: Parse PullMessagesResponse into motion events
items.facts: For each NotificationMessage: Topic text; inner tt:Message UtcTime attribute (UTC, fractional seconds allowed); active from SimpleItem IsMotion (or State) in tt:Data, values true/1 and false/0 (case-insensitive), anything else is ignored. Source and Data SimpleItems kept as extras. Missing UtcTime uses now. Garbage input returns an empty list and never throws. Topics seen: tns1:RuleEngine/CellMotionDetector/Motion (IsMotion) and tns1:VideoSource/MotionAlarm (State). Person/vehicle topics on some firmware are not captured in the Windows tests: accept any topic with IsMotion/State and keep the topic string so TV can filter later.

items.title: WS-Security UsernameToken digest
items.facts: Header Security (mustUnderstand=1) with UsernameToken: Username, Password Type=...#PasswordDigest = base64(sha1(nonce_raw + created_utf8 + password_utf8)), Nonce = base64(nonce) EncodingType Base64Binary, Created UTC 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ'. Nonce is 16 random bytes per call. Plaintext password never appears in the XML. Password is the camera (third) account password, not the TP-Link ID password. Envelope is SOAP 1.2; SOAP Fault becomes a device error; HTTP 401 without SOAP body is an auth error. Camera clock skew can matter: Created uses the TV clock (open question).

items.title: WS-Discovery and capabilities (optional)
items.facts: Probe for dn:NetworkVideoTransmitter to UDP multicast 239.255.255.250:3702, sent twice 0.3 s apart on every local IPv4 interface; ProbeMatches parsed for XAddrs and onvif://www.onvif.org/name/ scope. TCP scan of a subnet on port 2020 is the fallback. TV already finds cameras by TDP 20002, so ONVIF discovery is not needed; the host comes from the TDP match.

items.title: ONVIF PTZ (out of this lane)
items.facts: PTZ over ONVIF needs the camera account; the main app controls PTZ through the control channel. Left for the control lane.

decisions: D1 P0 is SD playback of a chosen day: day list -> clip list (with -71103 fallback) -> one range get playback over :8800 (LAN) or relay streamType 1 (remote/shared) -> plain MPEG-TS to ExoPlayer through the loopback bridge. Seek = new range request (new relay slot when remote).

D2 Use only the verified request: scale 1/1, event_type [1,2], string times; speed is client-side pacing, so the TV needs a PTS-aware pacer between the camera and ExoPlayer (ExoPlayer cannot be trusted to pace faster-than-real-time TS). Pacing and position mapping live in Kotlin next to RelayBridge, with the pure PTS/timeline logic in Dart for Tier 1 tests, or fully in Kotlin with Kotlin unit tests (to decide in implementation).

D3 Motion notifications default to polling getLastAlarmInfo (5 s on LAN, 30 s cloud-routed); ONVIF PullPoint is optional and only when the user stores a camera account. No cloud push is used by Windows.

D4 Clip day window uses the TV's local timezone midnight; a day on the day list uses the camera's own dates, mismatch possible near midnight if the TV timezone differs from the camera's (open question).
D5 Download is out of scope for TV P0 (tier 4).
D6 Shared cameras (role 1) never log in locally and always go through relay VOD and cloud passthrough search.
open_questions: Q1 Playback across clip boundaries, end of recordings and 2x/4x/8x are not verified on hardware (AGENTS.md section 8): can the TV rely on stream_status finished, or only on connection close?
Q2 Does ExoPlayer tolerate the TS discontinuities between recording files, or must the bridge insert discontinuity handling / restart the player per clip?
Q3 Day boundaries: does the camera interpret the searchDateWithVideo days in its own timezone while the TV queries clips in the TV timezone? Windows assumes they match.
Q4 Cloud passthrough searchDateWithVideo/searchVideoWithUTC for shared cameras: which commands a shared user may send is unverified.
Q5 Person/vehicle ONVIF topic names are unverified (no Windows test sample); only IsMotion/State on the motion topics are covered.
Q6 getLastAlarmInfo poll cadence for remote cameras (30 s) means up to 30 s delay; is the cloud passthrough rate limit known? Unknown per spec remote.control.rate_limits.
Q7 Should motion events trigger a relay live PiP (costs a media session) or only a toast? Windows only toasts.
Q8 The Windows stop request in relay_vod.py uses stop 'null' while the spec says stop 'playback'; which does real firmware accept?
Q9 Existing TV baseline (Topo TV) has relay live only: lib/api/vod_client.dart, lib/screens/vod_timeline_screen.dart, lib/ui/motion_pip_toast.dart do not exist yet and must be created.
